title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a stratified space whose strata are indexed by a finite poset I. X^*_i is the open stratum and X_i its closure. T_i is a tubular (conical) neighbourhood of X_i, with interior \mathring T_i. For a flag d = (i_0<...<i_n), \Sigma_d is the 'déploiement' piece: the iterated link-bundle or corner piece. The neighbouring pages index covers by Drap(I) and Drap^L_J(I). The heading 'Σ_J ou Σ_{J,L}' announces two generalisations of the one-index pieces Σ_i: one indexed by a band J, one by a pair of bands J<L. A 'bande' is a convex subset of I.

Definition. For a band J ⊂ I, let \bar J = {i | ∃ j∈J, i≤j} be the ideal generated by J. Note X_J := ∪_{j∈J} X_j = X^*_{\bar J} ⊃ X^*_J. Grothendieck sets
  Σ_J = X^*_J \ (X^*_J ∩ ∪_{i∈\bar J\J} \mathring T_i).
This is the locally closed union of the J-strata with open tubes around the lower boundary strata removed. It is a compact 'manifold-with-corners-like' stratified piece.

Formal properties (71):
- Σ_∅ = ∅, Σ_{{j}} = Σ_j and Σ_I = X.
- Σ_J = X_J when J is an ideal, since nothing is removed.

Gluing formula (generalising his earlier (72)):
  Σ_J ≅ colim(Σ_j, Σ_{ij}; a_{ij}: Σ_{ij}→Σ_i, b_{ij}: Σ_{ij}→Σ_j), for i,j ∈ J,
  ≅ colim_{d∈Dr_p(J)} Σ_d.
Here a_{ij} is the link-bundle projection and b_{ij} the inclusion into the boundary of Σ_j. Gluing Σ_j to Σ_i along the projection of its boundary collar reproduces the space up to homeomorphism, because the collar absorbs the mapping cylinder of a_{ij}. A marginal NB says Σ_J is also such a colimit over flags with entries allowed in I.

Homotopy statement (73): Σ_J ↪ X^*_J is a homotopy equivalence. Removing open collars, i.e. conical tubes, is a deformation retract.

Boundary (74):
  \dot Σ_J = X_J ∩ ∂T_{\bar J\J}, where T_{\bar J\J} = ∪_{i∈\bar J\J} T_i.
It is described as a union of images Im(Σ_{ij}→Σ_j), and as a colimit of Σ_d over flags of length ≥2 with an extra condition (illegible).

Marginal programme. A 'more economical' viewpoint: take the gluing formulas X = colim_{d∈Dr_p(I)} Σ_d as primary. One would then define Σ_i, Σ_{ij}, Σ_J and \dot Σ_J directly from the system of pieces, rather than as subsets of X. That is, describe a stratified space by its déploiement, a diagram of manifolds-with-corners indexed by flags.

Purpose. These are the building blocks for the next page: the tubular neighbourhood of Σ_J in Σ_{J'}, and the definition of Σ_{J,L} as \mathring T_J ∩ Σ_L. The overall aim is to show a tame stratified space is reconstructible from, and equivalent to, its unfolding (the 'déploiement' of the title and of Esquisse §5).
errors: (74): as transcribed, the boundary is a union of Im(Σ_{ij}→Σ_j) over i<j with i,j∈J. But the boundary of Σ_J comes from the removed tubes, i.e. i ∈ \bar J\J and j ∈ J. Images with both indices in J are interior gluing loci. Either the index condition is a slip or the reading is wrong; the image is ambiguous.

Equation numbers (71)-(74) clash with (70)-(73) on the previous sheet (numbered 38). This sheet (16) belongs to a different numbering run, so cross-references such as 'généralisation de (72)' refer to this run, not to page 38.

The homotopy equivalence (73) and the gluing isomorphisms are asserted without proof. They require tame tube systems (Thom–Mather control data, compatible collars), which are presupposed rather than established here.

missed.claim: The page records explicit gluing formulas for Grothendieck's déploiement, of which Esquisse §5 gives only a verbal sketch. These are the pieces Σ_J for arbitrary bands J (not just single strata), their colimit presentation over Dr(J), and their boundaries. The band-indexed (and next-page pair-of-bands Σ_{J,L}) formalism is a finer bookkeeping than the usual one-stratum-at-a-time unfoldings. It is essentially what later appears in Ayala–Francis–Tanaka's unzip and Lurie's exit-path setting, but not credited to Grothendieck.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is documentary evidence of how concretely Grothendieck carried out the Esquisse §5 déploiement programme. The convex-band indexing could streamline proofs of the 'stratified space ≃ diagram of manifolds with corners over flags' equivalence. Mathematically it is close to the known theory, so novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: These are concrete, unpublished working details of the déploiement sketched in Esquisse §5: band-indexed pieces, colimit over flags, homotopy equivalence and boundary formula. The mathematics itself is close to the later Thom–Mather/Verona/Ayala–Francis–Tanaka theory and largely routine once tubes are given.
transcription_corrections: '[J partie] bornée de I' should read approximately 'Soit J une bande de I' (convex subset), consistent with 'bandes' on the next page.
The NB on X_J: the parenthetical should be '(= ∪_{j∈\bar J} X^*_j = X^*_{\bar J} ⊃ X^*_J)'; the ideal \bar J, not J, indexes the open strata.

The top marginal note reads roughly: 'Un point de vue plus économique pour définir les Σ_i, Σ_ij, Σ_J, \dot Σ_J est alors de [les] déduire [...] (70) uniquement [à partir] des formules du type X = lim→_{d∈Dr_p(I)} Σ_d; soit Σ_i point de vue et non Σ_i ⊂ X^*_i, Σ_J ⊂ X^*_J ...'.
Index conditions in (74) are uncertain in the image; the boundary should involve i ∈ \bar J\J, j ∈ J.
